1|# Handoff 01 - Claude: cross-model tests for `c3 work`
2|
3|Date: 2026-10-29. Base commit: `0b712c4` (clean).
4|
5|## Question
6|
7|The operator wants GLM (`ZAI-claude :: glm-5.3`) as the main code author through `c3 work`, and
8|wants the TESTS for a change written by a model of a different family than the author. Should c3
9|itself grow support for this (and if so what exactly), or does it stay a coordinator convention
10|over two plain `c3 work` runs? Whatever we build becomes the default pipeline for every worker
11|task, so the shape is expensive to change later.
12|
13|## Task state
14|
15|- Done: `c3 work` (design `docs/work-mode.md`, README "Worker runs"). Engines claude (GLM-5.3,
16|  GLM-5.3-flash, DeepSeek-4.1-flash), codex (gpt-6.1-sol), muse (spark-1.3-contributor). One live
17|  work run per task. Record `.collab/<task>/work/<NN>-<provider>-<model>/` with brief.md,
18|  events.jsonl, report.md, diff.txt (git status before/after + diff --stat, computed by c3),
19|  run.json. Default allow list `Bash(cargo test|check|clippy|fmt:*)`; git refused; `--unrestricted`
20|  opt-in. First real GLM run (`.collab/c3-work/work/01-ZAI-claude-glm-5.3/report.md`) wrote 4
21|  integration tests and found/fixed a real guard-ordering bug; workspace tests/clippy/fmt green.
22|- Open: nothing in c3 today knows that two work runs belong together, which run is "author" and
23|  which is "tester", or which files each may touch.
24|- Not in scope: reviews/panels (unchanged), multi-host, cloud mode.
25|- Constraints: Windows host; full cargo test only with `-j 2` and never beside another build (OOM);
26|  z.ai/Muse/Grok expose no quota API; C3 never commits.
27|
28|## Coordinator's position (one opinion on the table, not the answer)
29|
30|One task = one author. Different models add value in review and in an INDEPENDENT oracle (tests),
31|not in relay-editing the same code. Fixes go back to the same author session.
32|
33|## Alternatives weighed
34|
35|1. **Convention only** - coordinator runs `c3 work` twice (author, then tester on another
36|   provider) and arbitrates by hand. Zero code; no enforcement, no linked record, no telemetry.
37|2. **Sighted tester** - `c3 work --role tests --of <work-id>`: the tester gets the author's brief
38|   + diff, c3 refuses a same-family tester, a path guard limits it to test files (`tests/`,
39|   `#[cfg(test)]` modules are a problem: they live inside src files).
40|3. **Blind / spec-first** - tester writes tests from the SPEC before or without seeing the
41|   implementation; author must make them pass and may not edit the test files (c3 checks
42|   diff.txt against a path scope and refuses/flags the run).
43|4. **Validity gate** - whichever of 2/3, c3 also proves the tests bite: they must fail on the
44|   base commit (or with the author's change reverted in a scratch worktree) and pass after.
45|
46|Current preference: 3 + 4 for features with a clear contract, 2 for bug fixes / refactors;
47|minimal c3 surface (linkage + path scope + validity gate), arbitration stays with the coordinator.
48|
49|## Questions
50|
51|- **Q1.** Is cross-model test authoring worth building into c3 at all, vs alternative 1? What
52|  evidence would change your answer?
53|- **Q2.** Blind (spec-first) vs sighted tester: which catches more real bugs, and where does each
54|  fail (over-fitting to the implementation vs testing a misread spec)?
55|- **Q3.** When a cross-model test fails, who decides "code bug" vs "test bug", and what must c3
56|  record so that decision is auditable? Can c3 help (e.g. re-run, revert-check) without deciding?
57|- **Q4.** The minimal c3 surface: flags, record linkage, path scope, validity gate - what is
58|  essential for v1 and what is gold-plating? How does it interact with "one live work run per
59|  task" and with `#[cfg(test)]` modules inside source files?
60|- **Q5.** Family-diversity rule: which pairings on this roster (GLM, DeepSeek, gpt-6.1-sol, Muse)
61|  make sense as author/tester, and should c3 enforce "different family" or only warn?
62|- **Q6.** Risks we have not listed (cost on monthly-capped plans, tests that pass trivially,
63|  tester rewriting the API, flaky tests on Windows, prompt-injection through the author's diff).
64|
65|Answer by number. Keep it under 900 words.

1|# `c3 work` — a worker run (design v1, 2026-10-20)
2|
3|Operator decision (2026-10-20): besides reviews and panels, `c3` must be able to run a roster
4|model as an ordinary CODING WORKER for low-stakes or test work: the model reads and edits the
5|repository, runs the test command it is allowed, and reports. First workers: GLM-5.3,
6|GLM-5.3-flash (z.ai endpoint), DeepSeek-4.1-flash (byteplus endpoint) — all through the `claude`
7|engine, which already drives them for reviews. Nothing about reviews changes.
8|
9|## Command
10|
11|```
12|c3 work --task <slug> --brief <file> --provider <roster label> [--model <id>]
13|        [--prompt <text>] [--effort low|medium|high|xhigh] [--max-turns <n>=80]
14|        [--timeout-sec <s>=3600] [--allow <tool pattern>]... [--collab-dir <dir>=.collab]
15|        [--detach] [--status [--id <id>]] [--wait [--id <id>] [--wait-timeout-sec <s>]]
16|        [--max-resumes <n>=3] [--quota-window-sec <s>] [--unrestricted]
17|```
18|
19|- `--provider` names a roster entry with `"engine": "claude"` and `"roles"` containing
20|  `"worker"` (the EXISTING `roles` key — no roster schema change). `--model` overrides the
21|  entry's model id (same endpoint). Any other entry is refused with the list of worker entries;
22|  an entry with another engine is refused in v1 ("workers run on the claude engine only").
23|- `--allow` adds Claude Code `--allowedTools` patterns (repeatable), e.g.
24|  `--allow "Bash(cargo test:*)"`. Default allow list: `Bash(cargo test:*)`, `Bash(cargo check:*)`,
25|  `Bash(cargo clippy:*)`, `Bash(cargo fmt:*)`. `Bash(git:*)` is REFUSED on the command line: a
26|  worker never commits.
27|- One live work run per task; a second `c3 work` on the same task is refused while one runs.
28|- The prompt on stdin = a fixed worker preamble + the brief file + `--prompt`. Preamble (verbatim
29|  in the code, tested):
30|  > You are a coding worker inside this repository. Do only what the brief asks, touch only the
31|  > files it names or clearly implies, never run git, never leave the repository, and never
32|  > commit. Finish with a final report: what you changed (file list), the exact test commands you
33|  > ran and their result counts, any deviation from the brief and why, and what you could not do.
34|  The prompt is refused above 1 MiB (the engine's `MAX_PROMPT_BYTES`).
35|
36|## The child
37|
38|Argv (built by a pure function with a unit test, like `claude_args`):
39|
40|```
41|claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands
42|       --permission-mode acceptEdits --tools Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob,Bash
43|       --allowedTools <allow list joined by ','> --model <id> [--effort <e>]
44|       --max-turns <n> --session-id <uuid>
45|```
46|
47|No `--restricted` (it would remove the write tools). Environment: exactly the endpoint route the
48|review engine uses — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (the value of the entry's
49|`env_key`, read at launch, never logged), `API_TIMEOUT_MS`; host markers scrubbed
50|(`c3_core::host::host_marker_names()`, recorded by NAME in `run.json` as `child_env_scrubbed`);
51|`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` as for reviews. Reuse the engine's launcher
52|discovery (`lineage::launcher_names` / `install_launchers`) and the endpoint environment builder
53|in `engines/claude_auth.rs` rather than writing a second one. The prompt travels on stdin.
54|
55|## The record
56|
57|`<collab-dir>/<task>/work/<NN>-<provider>-<model>/` (NN = 2-digit sequence per task):
58|
59|- `brief.md` — the prompt as sent (preamble + brief + `--prompt`).
60|- `events.jsonl` — the child's raw stream, **retained verbatim**, and may contain whatever the
61|  child printed (including a credential the child itself emitted), exactly like a consult's events
62|  file. It is the one record artifact that is NOT sanitized.
63|- **Writer contract (0.2.4, F93-1):** `run.json` is written only by its owning process (the c3
64|  process that claimed the record, writing its own live record) or under the task admission lock
65|  after a re-read; a reader never writes. The status/`--wait`/resume readers persist a dead owner's
66|  `died` transition only through the locked recovery (`recover_dead_run`), which re-reads and
67|  refuses to overwrite a newer generation.
68|- **Secret contract (0.2.4, F89-5):** `run.json`, `report.md` and `diff.txt` pass the project's
69|  single sanitizer (the pack redactor — 12 secret kinds plus an entropy pass); secret-shaped
70|  values are redacted with `[REDACTED:<kind>]`, the same rules as a pack. `events.jsonl` is the
71|  child's raw stream and is kept as-is. (The usage allow list and the argv grammar remove the most
72|  likely leak paths; the sanitizer is the catch-all for the report text.)
73|- `report.md` — the final assistant text (the `result` event's text; the last assistant text if
74|  the run died).
75|- `diff.txt` — `git status --short` before the run (the baseline) and after, plus
76|  `git diff --stat` after; computed by c3, not by the worker.
77|- `run.json` — `{task, seq, provider, model, engine:"claude", argv (no secrets — every `--allow`
78|  value is validated by the grammar below, so no free text travels there), child_env_scrubbed,
79|  started, ended, exit_code, status, pid + pid_start (the owning process — see Liveness), attempt,
80|  max_resumes, quota_window_sec, unrestricted, permission, turns, tool_calls: {Read, Edit, Write,
81|  Bash, ...}, files_changed: [...], usage, error}`. `status` is one of `done | died | timeout |
82|  refused | quota | running | waiting_quota | artifact_error`. `usage` is **rebuilt from an allow
83|  list of numeric counters** (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`,
84|  `cache_read_input_tokens`, `total_cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `num_turns`, and the codex/muse token

148|## Quota, resume and the alarm (0.2.3)
149|
150|A worker that runs out of its provider's usage limit is not a failure: it is paused and resumed
151|when the window reopens. The operator's wording: "we leave GLM writing code, it runs out of its
152|limits, they come back when the 5-hour cycle refreshes — at that moment nudge it so it starts
153|again."
154|
155|- **Classification.** After the child ends, a rejecting `rate_limit_event`, or a result/stderr
156|  matching the quota wording, makes the status `quota` (not `died`). The detection is the review
157|  engine's own `quota_evidence` (`engines/claude.rs`), so a worker and a reviewer read one wording
158|  and one regex. `run.json` gains `quota: {text, reset_at: <RFC3339 utc or null>, resume_at:
159|  <RFC3339 utc>, resumes: <n>, exhausted: <bool>}`. `resume_at` = `reset_at` + 60 s when the
160|  provider gave a reset time, else now + `--quota-window-sec` (default 18000 = 5 h; a roster
161|  entry's `ext.quota_window_sec` overrides the default).
162|- **`--resume [<id>]`** (same `--task`): the run must be `quota` or `timeout`. c3 relaunches the
163|  child with the same argv but `claude --resume <session-id>` instead of `--session-id`, the prompt
164|  on stdin "Your usage limit has reset. Continue the brief from where you stopped; do not redo
165|  finished steps; finish with the final report." (the brief is NOT re-sent — the session has it).
166|  The attempt is appended to `events.jsonl` after a `{"type":"c3","subtype":"resume","n":<k>,
167|  "at":<utc>}` separator; `report.md`/`diff.txt`/`run.json` are recomputed over the whole record;
168|  `quota.resumes` increments. Resumes are capped by `--max-resumes` (default 3); past the cap the
169|  status stays `quota` with `exhausted: true`. The effective `max_resumes` and `quota_window_sec`
170|  are persisted in `run.json` at the first run and reused by a later plain `--resume` (an explicit
171|  flag still overrides), so following the printed `--resume` line never silently resets a custom
172|  cap (0.2.4, F89-6).
173|- **The alarm (detached runs).** The background does NOT exit on quota. It writes status
174|  `waiting_quota` with `quota.resume_at`, sleeps in 30 s slices until then (checking a kick file
175|  `<record dir>/.kick` each slice), then resumes in-process; it repeats on a further quota hit up
176|  to the cap. The liveness check treats `waiting_quota` like `running` (the background pid is
177|  alive), so `--status` reads it as running (exit 2) and the one-live-run guard still holds.
178|- **`--kick [--id <id>]`.** On a `waiting_quota` run it creates the kick file (the sleeper resumes
179|  at once). On a foreground `quota` run (no sleeper) it resumes directly — so `--kick` is a
180|  one-word "try now" in both cases. On any other run it refuses with the state.
181|- **Foreground runs** on quota print the `resume_at` time and the exact `c3 work --task <t>
182|  --resume <id>` line, exit code 3. `--status`: `waiting_quota until <local time> (resume
183|  <n>/<max>)` plus the `quota` line; exit codes — `waiting_quota` counts as running (2), a `quota`
184|  run (exhausted or not) needs a hand (1). `--wait` keeps waiting through `waiting_quota`.
185|- **Secrets.** Nothing new is logged; the resume reuses the first launch's endpoint environment.

238|**`--allow` applies to claude only** (it maps to Claude Code `--allowedTools`); `run.json`'s

243|**The allow-list grammar (0.2.4, F89-4).** Without `--unrestricted`, every operator `--allow`
244|pattern must match `<Tool>`, `<Tool>(<exe>)` or `<Tool>(<exe>:*)` where `<exe>` is a plain
245|executable name `[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+`, optionally followed by plain subcommand words of the same
246|alphabet separated by single spaces (`Bash(cargo test:*)`, `Bash(npm run lint:*)`; a word never
247|starts with `-`, so `Bash(python -c:*)` is refused; no `*`, no quotes, no shell operators), and the
248|executable is not one of
249|`git`, `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `pwsh`, `powershell`, `cmd`. `Bash(*)`, `*`, `Bash(python -c:*)` and
